4. The root cause can be one value or many values of that column. Include every value that materially drives the change, and nothing else.
5. Answer.

{"resource": [{"name": "<resource name>", "type": "<resource type>"}]}

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df['dt'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
d = df[df['account_id']=='tVENWJP']
base = d[d['dt'] < '2025-09-20']
anom = d[d['dt'] == '2025-09-20']
print('Total change:', round(anom['unblended_cost'].sum() - base['unblended_cost'].mean(), 2))
for col in ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']:
    b = base.groupby(col)['unblended_cost'].mean()
    a = anom.groupby(col)['unblended_cost'].sum()
    ch = (a - b).dropna().sort_values()
    tot = ch.sum()
    print('\n===', col, '=== total explained:', round(tot,2))
    # show values with nonzero-ish change
    nz = ch[abs(ch) > 1.0]
    print(nz.round(2).to_string())
    # also check values present only on anomaly date
    print('only-anom values:', [v for v in a.index if v not in b.index])
    print('only-base values:', [v for v in b.index if v not in a.index])
